newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cemex and Apasco cut wholesale discounts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cemex and Apasco cut wholesale discounts.

text.p: Mexico's two leading cement makers, Cemex and Apasco, have decided to cut or eliminate discounts and thus raise domestic wholesale prices by 15 percent to 20 percent, one company source told Reuters on Thursday.
A director of one of the companies, who asked not to be identified, said price increases had begun to take effect on Monday.

"The effect has indeed taken place, cement (prices) will indeed increase, with the aim of being nationwide. We are either eliminating or reducing, as the case may be, the percentage discount we were offering to distributors," the director said by telephone.

The director said wholesale increases were not necessarily equivalent to retail price rises, which need to be approved by the Trade Ministry, which takes its lead from agreements between producers and the National Cement Chamber.

"In July (1996), there was a 17 percent increase in listed prices, but the market did not absorb the increase over the following months. Eliminating these discounts holds (the price) steady in dollar terms at $77-78 per tonne," he said.
Cemex and Apasco held market shares of 60.6 percent and 22.5 percent, respectively, of the Mexican market as of the third quarter of 1996.
